es: Ofrecer retroalimentación tras una derrota: reconocer un esfuerzo concreto, señalar una crítica específica y cerrar con el siguiente paso como pregunta de coaching.

teaching.en: I know the defeat hurts, and you have every right to feel disappointed.
teaching.es: Sé que la derrota duele y tienes todo el derecho a sentirte decepcionado.
teaching.explanationEs: Empieza reconociendo la emoción: así te escuchan antes de oír la crítica.
segments: I know the defeat hurts, and you
have every right to feel disappointed.
teaching.audioText: I know the defeat hurts, and you have every right to feel disappointed.

teaching.en: Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half.
teaching.es: A pesar de la derrota, estoy orgulloso de cómo defendisteis en la segunda parte.
teaching.explanationEs: Despite + sustantivo (sin of); proud of + el esfuerzo concreto.
segments: Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how
you defended in the second half.
teaching.audioText: Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half.

teaching.en: However, we lost the ball too often in the middle.
teaching.es: Sin embargo, perdimos el balón demasiadas veces en el medio.
teaching.explanationEs: However + coma: una crítica concreta y limitada a una cosa.
teaching.audioText: However, we lost the ball too often in the middle.

teaching.en: After this setback, what will it take for us to bounce back next Saturday?
teaching.es: Tras este contratiempo, ¿qué hará falta para que nos recuperemos el próximo sábado?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta de coaching que proyecta el siguiente paso.
segments: After this setback, what will it take
for us to bounce back next Saturday?
teaching.audioText: After this setback, what will it take for us to bounce back next Saturday?

teaching.en: This was a tough result, but you deserve credit for your effort.
teaching.es: Fue un resultado duro, pero mereces reconocimiento por tu esfuerzo.
teaching.explanationEs: Deserve credit for: reconocer el esfuerzo aunque se pierda.
segments: This was a tough result, but
you deserve credit for your effort.
teaching.audioText: This was a tough result, but you deserve credit for your effort.

teaching.en: It is only a setback; it is not the end of the season.
teaching.es: Es solo un contratiempo; no es el final de la temporada.
teaching.explanationEs: Setback: un problema temporal; ayuda a poner la derrota en perspectiva.
segments: It is only a setback; it is
not the end of the season.
teaching.audioText: It is only a setback; it is not the end of the season.

origin.text: Tu equipo perdió 2-1. Escribe una frase que reconozca un esfuerzo concreto (la defensa en la segunda parte) y continúe con however y una crítica concreta (perdieron el balón en el medio).

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dice el entrenador.

choices.text: He says the result was excellent.
He blames the players for the loss.
He says the players earned respect despite the loss.

feedback.es: Reconoce el esfuerzo aunque el resultado fuera duro.

origin.audio: It was a tough result, but you deserve credit for your effort.

prompt.es: Escribe la charla del entrenador tras la derrota.

answer.text:
Team, sit down for a moment. I know the defeat hurts, and you have every right to feel disappointed. I feel the same.
First, I want to say what I saw. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. Mia, your two tackles saved us three times, and Tom, you never stopped talking to the team. That is what a real captain does.
However, we lost the ball too often in the middle of the pitch, and that gave them the chance to score. It is only one thing, and it is fixable. It is not the end of the season.
So let me ask you: what would it take for us to keep the ball longer next Saturday? What could we try in training on Thursday? I would like to hear two ideas from each of you.
Remember, this is a tough result, but you deserve credit for your effort. Go home, rest, and come back ready to learn. I believe in this team.
accepted:
Team, sit down for a moment. I know the defeat hurts, and you have every right to feel disappointed. I feel the same.
First, I want to say what I saw. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. Mia, your two tackles saved us three times, and Tom, you never stopped talking to the team. That is what a real captain does.
However, we lost the ball too often in the middle of the pitch, and that gave them the chance to score. It is only one thing, and it is fixable. It is not the end of the season.
So let me ask you: what would it take for us to keep the ball longer next Saturday? What could we try in training on Thursday? I would like to hear two ideas from each of you.
Remember, this is a tough result, but you deserve credit for your effort. Go home, rest, and come back ready to learn. I believe in this team.

Everyone, come here. I know how painful this defeat is, and I understand you are disappointed. I am too.
I want to start with what worked. I'm proud of how you supported each other during the last twenty minutes. Leo, your effort in defence was excellent, and Sara, you encouraged everybody until the final whistle.
However, we passed only to the left side, and they closed that space easily. That is one concrete thing to improve, and it is not a disaster.
Now, what would help us to use the whole field next week? What is stopping us from looking for the right side? What could we try first on Tuesday? Think about it tonight, and tell me tomorrow.
It was a tough day, but you deserve to be proud of your effort. We will bounce back, and I will be with you on Saturday.

feedback.es: Una buena charla reconoce la emoción y dos esfuerzos concretos, hace una crítica específica con however y cierra con una pregunta de coaching.
